notable_absence.finding: The page states a concrete risk of the verification phase without an analyzer-context - 'the verification phase might drop documents that should have been returned as results due to lack of query context' - but this is a risk/warning, not a stable fact about the mechanism's normal operation, so it wasn't forced into a relation triple; recorded here as prose so it isn't lost. Same for the default-fallback rule: 'By default, the analyzer used for indexing the field (as per the index definition) will be picked up if no analyzer is specified in the analytic query' - a real default-value fact but about query-time behavior rather than a settings object, so it didn't fit hasDefaultValue's subject shape (a configurable setting) cleanly enough to force.

cross_component_finding: This page is the first in the batch to connect the Search Service to the Query service's own covering-index machinery: index:covering-index was previously documented only for GSI/query-service indexes (per the registry digest's own description: 'the relational property that holds between an index and a query when the index carries every field the query projects'). This page states the identical property in identical covering/non-covering terms for FULL-TEXT SEARCH indexes accessed via the SEARCH() SQL++ function - 'a full text search index can be described as one of the following: Covering index / Non-covering index.' Reused index:covering-index rather than minting a Search-specific duplicate, since the underlying relational property (does the index carry every field the query needs) is stated as literally the same concept, just applied to a new index kind - the page's own [Covering index] link points at the SAME indexes/covering-indexes.md page used for GSI indexes elsewhere in the docs.
